To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human fetal cortical subplate (SP, pioneer neurons) is spontaneously active in vivo and that the spontaneous cortical activity of human SP neurons is comprised of UP and DOWN states, similar to the adult neocortical slow oscillatory activity.

the spontaneous slow oscillation is a fundamental aspect (i.e., a “core” feature) of human cortical physiology, even at the very beginning of cortical development, and that it is generated by a small population of immature cortical neurons.
spontaneous cortical activity in the human fetal brain is similar to that of the adult brain, even though the neurons that generate this activity are very immature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the human cerebral cortex.
the development of human brain,
the development of the human cortex and the emergence of spontaneous electrical rhythms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spontaneous electrical activity of the human cortex in vitro is a fundamental aspect, which may be a fundamental aspect of the cortical network.
the UP/DOWN state is an intrinsic property of the developing human cortex, and it is not a consequence of sensory inputs.
the UP and DOWN states are not a fundamental aspect of cortical physiology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spontaneous slow oscillation is an intrinsic property of cortical neurons, and that this oscillation is present in a very immature ensemble (subplate neurons) as early as 18 gestational weeks.
human fetal cortex is not only a functional network but is also capable of generating a cortical slow oscillation.
the UP and DOWN states are generated by the immature cortex in the absence of sensory input, and that this fundamental cortical pattern is present in humans from midgestation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cortical UP and DOWN rhythms are a fundamental property of the human cortex and not a result of the adult brain’s maturation.
the UP and DOWN state rhythm of human cortical neurons is not a consequence of the adult morphology and physiology of the neocortex, but rather a developmental trait of the human fetal cortex.

the human fetal neocortex is already endowed with a complex intrinsic physiology that is not only similar to that of the adult neocortical network, but also essential for the normal maturation of the cortex.
